chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who raises his head from ruku' before the Imam: should he return and bow again if the Imam is slow, and then raise his head with him? He said: No.

So the proper understanding of this report is one of two things: one is that he is praying behind one whose leadership is not to be followed; in that case, it is not permissible for him to return to ruku', because that would become an addition in the salat. The second is that he did that deliberately; then likewise it is not permissible for him to return to ruku'. Rather, he should return only if he raised his head forgetfully, so that his raising of the head may coincide with the Imam's raising of the head.

key_terms.الرُّكُوعِ: ruku', the bowing posture in salat
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.زِيَادَةً: an addition to the salat beyond its prescribed form
key_terms.لَا يُقْتَدَى بِهِ: one whose leadership in prayer is not to be followed

ai.seo_question: If someone raises his head from ruku' before the Imam, should he go back down into ruku'?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a follower who raises his head from ruku' before the Imam. It states that he should not return to ruku' in cases where doing so would count as an improper addition to the salat, while return is appropriate when the act occurred forgetfully so that his motion aligns with the Imam.
